chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Ibrahim al-Karkhi, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, regarding:

A man who arrived in Makkah with his hady during the ten days—he said: if it is an obligatory hady, then he should not slaughter it except at Mina; and if it is not obligatory, then let him slaughter it in Makkah if he wishes. And if he had marked it and garlanded it, then he should not slaughter it except on the Day of al-Adha.

key_terms.أَشْعَرَهُ: he marked the sacrificial animal as dedicated
key_terms.بِمَكَّةَ: in Makkah, where a non-obligatory hady may be slaughtered
key_terms.بِمِنًى: at Mina, the designated place for certain hajj sacrifices
key_terms.قَلَّدَهُ: he garlanded the animal as a sign that it was designated for sacrifice
key_terms.هَدْيًا وَاجِبًا: an obligatory sacrificial offering that must be fulfilled according to legal duty
key_terms.يَوْمَ الْأَضْحَى: the Day of al-Adha, the appointed day for slaughter

ai.seo_question: Where should obligatory and non-obligatory hady be slaughtered during hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith states the legal ruling concerning the place and time of slaughtering the hady brought to Makkah during the first ten days of Dhu al-Hijjah. Obligatory hady must be slaughtered at Mina, while non-obligatory hady may be slaughtered in Makkah, and an animal that has been marked and garlanded is not to be slaughtered except on the Day of al-Adha.
